definitions.gloss: Rashomon (story by Akutagawa; film by Kurosawa)
definitions.explanation: A 1915 short story by {芥川龍之介|あくたがわりゅうのすけ}, set at the ruined main gate of the old capital Kyoto, where a jobless servant decides to become a thief. Also the title of Akira Kurosawa's 1950 film, which takes its setting from this story and its plot of conflicting testimonies from Akutagawa's {藪|やぶ}の{中|なか}.

notes:
CULTURAL NOTE:
- The story is read in almost every first-year high school Japanese class
- The real gate was the {羅城門|らじょうもん}, the southern gate of the Heian capital; {羅生門|らしょうもん} is the spelling of later tales and of Akutagawa
- English "the Rashomon effect" (witnesses telling contradictory versions of an event) comes from the film; Japanese speakers rarely use the phrase
